version.changelog:
No code or functionality changes in this release; only documentation updates.

- Documentation updated: SKILL.md now uses Chinese, adds metadata (version, author, license, tools), and clarifies usage and trigger instructions.
- No changes to files or logic; behavior remains unchanged.

llm.summary: This skill is narrowly aimed at OpenClaw session cleanup, but it under-discloses the risk of automatically deleting or rebuilding local session data.

dimensions.detail: Bash access and the OpenClaw sessions directory are related to the cleanup purpose, but that directory is a sensitive local agent data store and should be handled with explicit user control.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single Markdown skill with no bundled executable scripts, dependencies, remote payloads, or installer behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The shown commands are inspection-only, but the workflow is labeled automatic and safe/no-risk without confirmation, backup, age criteria, recovery steps, or clear limits for destructive cleanup.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact does not install persistence, services, hooks, or privilege-escalation mechanisms; the main concern is possible mutation or deletion of local session records.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent, but it advertises automatic cleanup, deletion of old cron sessions, and rebuilding sessions.json, which can affect private or important OpenClaw session history.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the cleanup steps before installing or invoking this skill. Only run destructive session cleanup after backing up the OpenClaw sessions directory and explicitly confirming what files will be deleted or how sessions.json will be rebuilt.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern: session cleanup is purpose-aligned, but calling the automatic workflow safe/no-risk materially under-discloses possible data loss from deletion or rebuild actions.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the Chinese-language instructions may reduce accessibility for some users, but they are not evidence of malicious or hidden behavior.
